task.description: Diagnose ISS-0433: identify every Application.get_env call in Scheduler.Poller's tick path, confirm which (if any) are genuinely tick-invariant, and convert only those to :persistent_term populated once at boot. Implement the fix if any qualifying call is found; report honestly if none qualifies.

result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS: NO QUALIFYING Application.get_env CALL EXISTS in Scheduler.Poller's tick path. No code change made -- this is a legitimate 'nothing to convert' outcome, not a shortfall.

Every Application.get_env call reachable from `Letflow.Scheduler.Poller.handle_info(:tick, _)` (poller.ex:100-124) was enumerated and individually checked against runtime-mutation evidence (grepped test files for `Application.put_env` on the same config keys, not just trusted the issue's framing):

1. `Application.get_env(:letflow, :alert_hooks, [])` -- poller.ex:149, inside `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`, called once per tick. `test/letflow/obs/alerts_test.exs:43,48` calls `Application.put_env(:letflow, :alert_hooks, overrides)` with an `on_exit` restore -- a test fixture that reconfigures this key at runtime without a BEAM restart. NOT tick-invariant.

2. `Application.get_env(:letflow, :ordering, [])` -- poller.ex:219, 234, 249, inside `maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1` respectively (three separate reads of the SAME key within one tick -- itself a smaller, separate redundancy not in scope here since none of the three qualifies for persistent_term anyway). `test/letflow/ordering_test.exs:40-41` calls `Application.put_env(:letflow, :ordering, Keyword.merge(base, overrides))` with an `on_exit` restore. NOT tick-invariant.

3. `Letflow.Scheduler.poll_interval_ms/0`, `jitter_ms/0`, `retention_enabled?/0`, `retention_due?/1` (called from `handle_info`/`schedule_next_tick`/`maybe_run_retention_sweep`, poller.ex:102,109,121,137,206,211) all read through `Letflow.Scheduler.scheduler_config/0` (scheduler.ex:548: `Application.get_env(:letflow, :scheduler, [])`) -- this is the 'hot per-tick path it calls into' the issue's own scope explicitly includes. `test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs:117-124` (`put_scheduler_config/1`, used by the file's own 'AC8: Poller.handle_info(:tick, _) reads config fresh and uses the overridden poll_interval_ms' describe block) and `test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs:194-201` both call `Application.put_env(:letflow, :scheduler, overrides)` with an `on_exit` restore. NOT tick-invariant.

This is not merely test-fixture incidental use -- poller.ex's own moduledoc (lines 22-24) documents this as an INTENTIONAL, load-bearing design property: 'Config (`config :letflow, :scheduler, [...]`, `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own accessors) is read fresh on every tick, so a runtime override (e.g. a test calling `Application.put_env/3`) takes effect on the very next tick.' AC8 in poller_test.exs exists specifically to assert this behavior (a timer armed after the Poller's first tick fires within the OVERRIDDEN interval, proving the very-next-tick freshness). Converting `:scheduler` to a boot-time `:persistent_term` snapshot would make AC8 and every other put_env-based override in poller_test.exs/scheduler_test.exs/ordering_test.exs/alerts_test.exs silently stale until a restart -- a behavior regression, not a safe optimization, and would falsify this issue's own step-2 confirmation instruction ('confirm each read value is genuinely tick-invariant... If you find a config value that IS legitimately changed at runtime... do NOT convert that one').

Searched for any non-test `Application.put_env` call on these three keys (`:scheduler`, `:ordering`, `:alert_hooks`) across `lib/` and `config/` to rule out the possibility that only test code (not production code) reconfigures them, which would not by itself disqualify a persistent_term conversion if the production runtime never mutates them -- but per this project's own conventions (poller.ex's moduledoc, and ISS-0432's own closing note calling this 'a still-unfiled persistent_term follow-up' rather than a confirmed action item) the deciding factor is the documented AND test-verified 'fresh every tick, override takes effect next tick' contract, which the test suite exercises as a genuine behavioral property of the running system, not merely test plumbing that could be pointed at a different persistent_term write path instead. No production code path calls Application.put_env on these keys (expected -- config is normally set once via config/*.exs), but that does not make the values tick-invariant in the sense this issue requires, because the documented contract is that a RUNTIME override (however it is invoked) takes effect without a restart, and persistent_term reads populated once at boot would break that contract outright, not just in tests.

CONCLUSION: All Application.get_env calls reachable from the Poller's tick path (poller.ex's own two direct call sites plus the one hot per-tick path it calls into, Letflow.Scheduler.scheduler_config/0) are confirmed, by direct grep evidence of Application.put_env against the identical keys in four test files plus the module's own moduledoc documenting this as intentional, to be legitimately runtime-mutable -- exactly the exclusion case ISS-0433's own acceptance criteria anticipates ('If you find a config value that IS legitimately changed at runtime... do NOT convert that one'). Zero calls qualify for :persistent_term conversion. No code was changed; no test was added (there is nothing to test -- ISS-0433's own AC requiring a test that persistent_term is set before first tick is inapplicable when no config value is being moved to persistent_term). `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` was not re-run since no file was touched. Routing to ORCH rather than REVIEWER because there is no diff for REVIEWER to gate -- ORCH should close ISS-0433 as no_defect (mirroring ISS-0432's own closing pattern) rather than route to CODE-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV. Not a tenant-data path either way: Poller iterates `Registration.schema_name` (platform-wide, non-tenant-scoped metadata) and the config keys examined are process-wide GenServer configuration, not tenant data -- SECURITY-REVIEWER gate correctly not applicable regardless of outcome.
result.recommendation_to_orch: Close ISS-0433 as no_defect: every Application.get_env call reachable from Scheduler.Poller's tick path (poller.ex:149 :alert_hooks, poller.ex:219/234/249 :ordering, and Letflow.Scheduler.scheduler_config/0 at scheduler.ex:548 for :scheduler, the latter being the 'hot per-tick path' the issue's own scope includes) is confirmed genuinely runtime-mutable via Application.put_env in test/letflow/obs/alerts_test.exs, test/letflow/ordering_test.exs, test/letflow/scheduler_test.exs, and test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs (AC8), all with on_exit restoration, matching an intentional documented contract in poller.ex's own moduledoc (lines 22-24) that config is read fresh every tick so a runtime override takes effect on the very next tick. No qualifying tick-invariant config value exists to move to :persistent_term. No code, test, or doc change was made on this branch; recommend closing without merging any diff (branch has no commits beyond step-00/step-01 handoffs). Do not route to CODE-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV -- there is nothing to design or implement. If ORCH still wants a durable record, treat this handoff's summary as the closing note, mirroring ISS-0432's own no_defect precedent.
